claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature single-phase BCC state.
Cooling Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from its high-temperature BCC state initiates local chemical ordering.
The cooling-induced local configurations include incipient B2-type arrangements.
Atomic-size and bonding differences among the alloying elements drive local chemical ordering.
Local chemical ordering lowers the alloy's free energy locally.
Cooling-induced local chemical order acts as a nucleation precursor for secondary ordered phases during later thermal exposure.
Nanoscale local chemical order evolves into incipient ordered domains within the BCC matrix.
As temperature decreases, atoms overcome local energy barriers and rearrange into chemically favorable configurations.
Early-stage local ordering creates compositional fluctuations.
The degree of local ordering and subsequent phase stability during annealing are sensitive to cooling rate.
Al and Cr promote local ordering through their atomic-size and bonding preferences.
Slow cooling allows substantially more atomic rearrangement and local ordering than rapid quenching.
After identical annealing, slow-cooled samples will have a higher fraction of ordered domains than rapidly quenched samples.
After identical annealing, ordered domains will be larger in slow-cooled samples than in rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will primarily retain metastable BCC structure with little local ordering.
Rapidly quenched samples will show little secondary-phase precipitation during subsequent thermal exposure.
The proposed mechanism should apply broadly to compositionally complex alloys having substantial atomic-size mismatch and bonding differences.
Simpler alloys lacking substantial atomic-size mismatch and bonding differences should exhibit less local ordering and a smaller effect on phase stability.
